Subject: Residency + delete certification questions for private/VPC deploy

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the demo earlier. We're moving the conversation with our InfoSec and Procurement teams toward a private deployment in our AWS account. A few concrete questions came up that I wanted to capture in writing so we can hand to procurement: 

1) Confirm that customer data (model inputs & outputs, KV caches, and generated artifacts) will only be stored in our AWS account S3 buckets or EBS volumes we control. Any metadata retained by Redwood for operational purposes — what does that look like and where is it stored?

2) If we request a tenant deletion, what are the end-to-end steps (for lack of better words, "prove delete")? Please include timing (RTO/RPO) for snapshots, backups, and any off-cluster replicas.

3) We require customer-managed KMS keys for encryption-at-rest. Does Redwood support BYOK for the Private package, and if so, how are key rotations and access audits logged?

4) For compliance: can you provide a template deletion report or attestation we can include in our contract?

Would appreciate a short written Q&A we can share internally. We're aiming to close the procurement review next week.

Attachments: none from us.

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of IT Security, Atlas Health

Samira —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers first; Marissa will add technical specifics below and Karthik will chime in on audit/SLA bits. I'll also attach a short "residency and deletion" package for procurement.

Short answers: 
- Customer-controlled storage: Yes — in a Private deployment we either run a tenant inside your AWS account (preferred) or in an isolated VPC dedicated to you; in both cases persistent storage (S3/EBS) can be owned and administered by you. Redwood does not retain a copy of customer data outside your configured buckets/volumes except for ephemeral logs/metrics as described below.
- Deletion / prove-delete: We provide a three-step deletion workflow: 1) logical data purge (application layer), 2) snapshot & object lifecycle purge (S3 object tombstoning + lifecycle expiration), 3) cryptographic key revocation for BYOK flows plus optional sanitization script for disks. Typical completion window is 72 hours for logical purge and lifecycle triggers; full removal from snapshots/backups depends on retention windows — we'll provide the exact SLA/mapping in the attachment.
- BYOK/KMS: Supported. You retain the CMK in your account; Redwood receives temporary grants scoped to the service principal. Rotations are customer-driven; we record key access in our audit logs and can forward audit events (CloudWatch/CloudTrail) for cross-checking.
- Attestation: We'll provide a template deletion certificate and a minimal evidence package (object list, snapshot ids, and audit checksums) that you can attach to procurement.

Next steps I propose: I will share the procurement package (short PDF + deletion-evidence template) and propose a 30-minute call with your InfoSec procurement folks tomorrow or Monday to walk through.

Jordan

Hi Samira —

Adding the technical detail Jordan promised so procurement/ops can see an ops-level view: 

- Where data lives: application writes are to S3 buckets and EBS volumes in your account under a prefix we agree on (e.g., s3://atlas-health-redwood/). KV cache (if enabled) uses ephemeral EBS mounts on hosts inside your VPC and is not written to durable storage by default. Logs: we stream non-sensitive operational logs to a customer-owned CloudWatch log group (or to an S3 bucket) when configured; debug-level traces that might contain customer payloads are explicitly disabled by default and require an approved runbook.

- Backups & snapshots: Periodic snapshots are customer-configured. For S3 we rely on lifecycle rules you configure; for EBS we recommend a 7-day snapshot window by default but can change. If you request immediate deletion, we will trigger a one-off lifecycle that expires objects and schedule EBS snapshot deletion and then provide snapshot IDs for verification. Note: some storage providers will retain data for a short grace window after delete to meet internal durability guarantees — we document these windows in the evidence package.

- Deletion proof artifacts we can produce: list of object prefixes deleted (CSV), snapshot ids and deletion timestamps, CloudTrail extract showing DeleteObject/DeleteSnapshot calls, and MD5 checksums of object manifests before/after removal. We include a short signed statement from Redwood operations that the steps were executed and a timestamped chain-of-custody log.

- BYOK flow: you create a CMK and grant the Redwood service principal a time-bound Encrypt/Decrypt grant. Access returns are visible in your CloudTrail; Redwood will also emit operation-level audit records (signed) to a designated S3 path. On key revocation we remove access and, by design, render any remaining ciphertext inaccessible.

I've attached the deletion-evidence-template.xlsx — it shows the fields procurement usually requests. Happy to adapt to whatever fields your legal team wants.

-Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks both — this is very helpful. A couple follow-ups from procurement/security: 

- Does Redwood provide a signed attestation template for deletion we can attach to the Master Services Agreement (MSA)? Ideally something that references the events we discussed and a Redwood ops sign-off practice.
- For the BYOK path, procurement wants to confirm that revoking the CMK will render all previously stored data irrecoverable by Redwood. You mention ciphertext being inaccessible; procurement would like that called out explicitly in the attestation.
- Can you indicate expected timelines: 1) logical purge completion (hours), 2) snapshot deletion (days), 3) guarantee of no external copies (weeks) or explain caveats.

If you can attach the attestation and an example of the CloudTrail extract we would be close to sharing with legal. Also please include any DocuSign link for the addendum if you have a standard one.

Best,
Samira

Subject: Re: Residency + delete certification questions for private/VPC deploy

Samira —

Uploaded the package and drafted a short attestation that calls out the BYOK behavior and the staged removal timeline. Key points in the attestation: 
- Logical purge: completed within 24 hours of request (application-level deletes initiated and confirmed).
- Snapshot/object lifecycle initiation: within 72 hours; complete removal depends on configured retention but we will trigger expedited lifecycle and provide evidence. Typical snapshot deletion completes within 7 days in our customers' observed runs; we list exceptions in the attestation (cloud-provider retention/grace periods).
- Cryptographic irrecoverability: When you revoke or rotate the CMK such that Redwood no longer has Decrypt privileges, any ciphertext encrypted with that key becomes unrecoverable by Redwood. We explicitly state this in the attestation.

I've attached: residency-overview.pdf, deletion-evidence-template.xlsx, and a KMS flow diagram (kms-diagram.png). Also included a draft DocuSign link for the addendum: https://docusign.com/atlascert/xyz123 (placeholder until legal redlines).
